Distinguish between the abstraction/interface package and the concrete implementation package.

Report file paths precisely.

content.text:
I have what I need. This is the `memos` Go project (module `github.com/usememos/memos`), and identity provider support lives under `internal/idp`.

## Findings

### 1. Abstraction package (interface / base types)

- **Package name:** `idp` (import path `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp`)
- **File:** `/bench/repo/internal/idp/idp.go`

This is the shared abstraction package. It defines the provider-agnostic `IdentityProviderUserInfo` struct (`Identifier`, `DisplayName`, `Email`, `AvatarURL`) that all concrete identity provider implementations return. It contains no protocol-specific logic — it is the common contract that concrete providers depend on.

### 2. Concrete protocol implementation package

- **Package name:** `oauth2` (import path `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp/oauth2`)
- **Files:**
  - `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go` (implementation)
  - `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2_test.go` (tests)

This is the concrete **OAuth2** protocol implementation. Its doc comment states: "Package oauth2 implements the OAuth2 identity provider integration." It defines an `IdentityProvider` type built from a `storepb.OAuth2Config`, with `NewIdentityProvider`, `ExchangeToken` (with PKCE support), and `UserInfo` (which returns the abstraction's `*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo`). It imports and depends on the abstraction package (`github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp`).

## Important clarifications

- **Single Go module.** The whole repo is one Go module (`github.com/usememos/memos`, see `/bench/repo/go.mod`). In Go, "packages" correspond to directories, so the abstraction and the implementation are separate Go packages, not separately-published dependency packages.
- **OAuth2 is the only concrete protocol implementation that ships.** `internal/idp` contains exactly two subpackages: `idp` (abstraction) and `oauth2` (implementation). There is no separate SAML, LDAP, or dedicated OIDC package — despite proto/config also referencing an `OIDC` identity provider type, the actual credential-exchange/user-info logic is implemented only in the `oauth2` package. (OIDC is layered on top of the generic OAuth2 flow.)

### Related (context, not the packages themselves)
- Protobuf service/config definitions: `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/idp_service.proto`, generated Go in `/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/idp_service.pb.go` and `/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/idp.pb.go` (the `OAuth2Config` used by the implementation lives in the generated `storepb`).
- Design doc: `/bench/repo/docs/plans/2026-04-21-sso-user-identity-linkage/`
